ops.title: desk-runner: a restarted landing runner replays settled release clocks, and the cut clock reads prose words as targets
ops.description:
Seen Oct 20, 1:32 PM, drive release-v3, right after the landing runner moved from 0.7.172 to 0.7.183 by TERM and restart (cci #104836).

1. Stale release clocks. On its first pass, the restarted landing runner replayed release clocks for monorepo #41074 and #41089. Both were released hours earlier. It posted 7 duplicate RELEASE-HELD blockers, cci #104815 to #104821. A restart has to rebuild clock state from the store and the drive's release records, so a settled release raises nothing.

2. Cut-clock target parsing. The cut clock takes prose words in a GO or release line, such as 'at', 'after', and 'head', as release targets. Example: CUT-SILENT release-walker-7 'after' (#104822). Targets must come from structured fields or the known target set, never from free text.

ops.text: A landing runner restarted mid-drive posts no RELEASE-HELD or other release-clock blocker for a release the drive already recorded as released
The cut clock never takes an English word like at, after, or head as a target; a test covers the release-walker-7 'after' case
